frontier.hypothesis: Region A closes iff the base pseudo's cse quantity carries NO constant, or carries one whose RTX code is REG or a bare PLUS -- because cse.c:5171-5176 is the only guard that skips the substitution. A `(const (plus sym K))` does NOT qualify (that is what `eda + 0x226` canonicalises to, which is exactly why session-1 K1 and its post-region-B re-measure both folded).
frontier.mechanism: fold_rtx's fast path for REG operands substitutes qty_const only when `GET_CODE (qty_const[...]) != REG && GET_CODE (qty_const[...]) != PLUS` (cse.c:5171-5176); qty_const is populated when a CONSTANT_P value enters the register's equivalence class (cse.c:1377-1397).
frontier.next_probe: Find a MATCHED sibling that already emits register+displacement addressing off a symbol base and read what its base pseudo's quantity looks like. Cheap locator: `grep -l '[0-9]\+(\$s[0-9])' asm/funcs/*.s` intersected with the zero-rule / non-queued function set, then `-da` that sibling's TU and compare its `.cse` around the base pseudo with func_8003B9D0's insn 89. The sibling's C spelling is the answer; do not guess it.

frontier.hypothesis: A small standalone reproduction will find the pointer-initialisation spelling that keeps `(mem (plus (reg) (const_int 1100)))` far faster than sandbox round-trips on the real file.
frontier.mechanism: Region A is entirely local to one cse decision about one pseudo, so it reproduces in a ~40-line TU; the gradient is readable directly in the `-da` `.cse` dump (folded vs unfolded MEM) with no scoring needed.
frontier.next_probe: Build tmp/grind/func_8003B9D0/s3/mini.c containing only the qf & 0x30 block's shape against a dummy extern s16 symbol, compile with the exact build flags plus `-da`, and sweep pointer-initialisation spellings, checking each `.cse` dump for whether insn N keeps `(mem:HI (plus (reg) (const_int 1100)))`. Port back only a spelling that keeps it, then re-measure with sandbox. Note regions A and B are NOT coupled (K7), so a region-A change can be evaluated on its own.

frontier.hypothesis: func_8003AFFC takes the D_800A3878 object pointer as an argument, and our zero-argument call is a decompilation error rather than a codegen choice.
frontier.mechanism: m2c infers the signature from $a0 being live and unreloaded across the call (tgt[48] sets it, tgt[68] is the jal); a genuine void-argument callee would not require that liveness.
frontier.next_probe: Read asm/funcs/func_8003AFFC.s to see whether it actually consumes $a0. If it does, correct the prototype and the call site (there are currently three duplicate `extern void func_8003AFFC(void);` declarations in src/code6cac_c2.c, at lines 73, 74 and 171, which should be reconciled to one) and re-measure. Expect byte-neutrality here; the value is correctness of the decompilation and of func_8003AFFC's own future grind.
